Why Prime Numbers Are Your Best Friend

A cell numbered "2" on a Shikaku grid is the strongest clue — it can only be a 1×2 or 2×1 rectangle, no thinking required. Start every puzzle by scanning for primes first. Then check if those rectangles reveal new forced placements for neighboring numbers. This "cascade from primes" technique works on every difficulty level and is the single fastest way to speed up your solving.

GridPaw: Free Shikaku Puzzle Game Online

GridPaw is a free Shikaku puzzle game with adorable cat visuals. Draw rectangles on a numbered grid so each rectangle covers exactly the number of cells shown. It's the classic Shikaku (rectangle partition) puzzle by Nikoli — the same company behind Sudoku — reimagined with cats.

Whether you're new to Shikaku or a seasoned solver, GridPaw offers unlimited procedurally generated puzzles across 7 difficulty levels, from Tutorial 4×4 to Legend 8×8. Every puzzle has a unique solution reachable by pure logic — no guessing required.

How to Play Shikaku

The rules of Shikaku are simple:

  • The grid contains several numbered cells.
  • Draw rectangles around each number so the area equals the number (a "4" needs a 1×4, 2×2, or 4×1).
  • Each rectangle contains exactly one number.
  • Rectangles cannot overlap, and every cell must be covered.

That's it — no math beyond multiplication. The challenge is figuring out which shapes fit where when multiple numbers compete for space.

Shikaku Difficulty Levels

  • Tutorial (4×4) — Learn the basics with guided hints (levels 1–3)
  • Beginner (4×5) — Gentle step up, build confidence (levels 4–7)
  • Easy (5×5) — Simple puzzles, perfect for beginners (levels 8–12)
  • Medium (5×6) — Introduces more complex rectangle shapes (levels 13–18)
  • Medium-Hard (6×6) — Requires multi-step reasoning (levels 19–25)
  • Hard (6×7) — Advanced deduction needed (levels 26–33)
  • Expert (7×7) — Deep logic chains (levels 34–42)
  • Master (7×8) — For experienced solvers (levels 43–52)
  • Legend (8×8) — The ultimate Shikaku challenge (level 53+)

Tips & Strategy

Rushing to fill cells is the fastest way to get stuck. Instead, work systematically:

  1. Start with primes. Numbers like 2, 3, 5, 7 can only form 1×N rectangles — their shape is forced.
  2. Work from corners. Boundary positions have fewer options, making them easier to resolve.
  3. Look for the largest number. Bigger numbers have fewer valid rectangle shapes.
  4. Eliminate by overlap. If a placement blocks another number, it's wrong.

Visit our Tips & Strategy page for detailed guides on each technique.

Common Shikaku Mistakes to Avoid

Forgetting area constraints: a rectangle around a "4" must cover exactly 4 cells — no more, no fewer. Overlapping rectangles: each cell belongs to exactly one rectangle. Ignoring forced placements: if a number can only fit one rectangle shape, place it first.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is GridPaw free to play?
Yes! GridPaw is completely free. No download, no account, no payment. Just open the page and start solving Shikaku puzzles.
What is a Shikaku puzzle?
Shikaku (also called rectangle partition) is a Japanese logic puzzle where you draw rectangles on a numbered grid. Each rectangle must contain exactly one number, and the rectangle's area must equal that number. GridPaw is the cat-themed version!
How is Shikaku different from Sudoku?
Both are logic puzzles, but Shikaku uses spatial reasoning (drawing rectangles) instead of number placement. If you like Sudoku's deduction, you'll enjoy Shikaku's area-based thinking.
Where should beginners start?
Start with the Tutorial level (4×4 grid) which teaches the rules step by step, then try Easy 5×5 puzzles. Check our How to Play guide for a complete walkthrough.
Does GridPaw have a daily challenge?
Yes! A new 6×6 Shikaku puzzle is generated every day at midnight UTC. Everyone worldwide gets the same puzzle. Track your streak and earn the Week Warrior badge at 7 consecutive days.
Can I play on my phone?
Yes! GridPaw works on any device with a browser. Drag to draw rectangles on desktop, or swipe on mobile. The grid automatically resizes to fit your screen.
What are the cat blocks?
When you correctly place a rectangle, it turns into a cute cat block with a random color and expression. There are 15 different cat expressions and 8 colors — no two rectangles look the same!
Is there a solver for when I'm stuck?
Yes! Visit the Online Solver page. Enter your puzzle's numbers and the solver will find the unique solution using backtracking.
How many levels are there?
Unlimited! GridPaw procedurally generates puzzles, so you'll never run out. There are 7 difficulty tiers from Tutorial (4×4) to Legend (8×8), plus a daily challenge.
